Requirement 03.03.01 — System Auditing
Create and retain system audit logs and records to the extent needed to enable the monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorized system activity.
03.03.01.a: Audit logs needed (i.e., event types to be logged) to enable the monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorized system activity are specified

Assessment objectives (a coverage checklist — do NOT copy their wording):
- audit logs needed (i.e., event types to be logged) to enable the monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorized system activity are specified

Evidence excerpts:
--- [IT-STD-014_Audit_Logging_Standard_v2.3.docx] (excerpt)
4.1 Required Event Types
The following event categories must be generated and forwarded to Graylog for all in-scope systems:
(a) Authentication: successful and failed logons, MFA challenges and denials, account lockouts (Okta System Log, Windows Event IDs 4624, 4625, 4740).
(b) Account management: user/group creation, deletion, privilege changes, admin role assignment (Okta, Google Workspace Admin audit, Event IDs 4720, 4728, 4732).
(c) Security tooling: SentinelOne threat detections, agent tamper or uninstall attempts, policy changes.
(d) Network: PA-440 traffic logs for deny actions, threat logs, GlobalProtect VPN sessions, and configuration commits.
(e) Data access: Google Drive external sharing changes and bulk downloads (>500 files/hour).
(f) Backup: Datto SIRIS job failures, retention changes, and restore actions.
The IT Security Lead reviews this list annually and after any major system change. Owner: IT Manager. Last reviewed 2024-03-18.

--- [CHG0041872_PA440_Log_Forwarding.pdf] (excerpt)
Change Request: CHG0041872
Requested by: Network Administrator | Approved by: IT Manager, CAB 2024-04-09
Summary: Update log forwarding profile "LF-Graylog-Std" on both PA-440 firewalls to match event types defined in Audit Logging Standard v2.3.
Implementation details:
- Traffic log: forward on Action = deny, drop, reset-both (previously all traffic; reduces volume ~70%)
- Threat log: all severities
- Config and System logs: forward all, via Device > Log Settings
- GlobalProtect: forward connect/disconnect and auth failures
- Syslog server profile "graylog-01" TCP 6514, BSD format
Validation: Test deny rule triggered from 10.20.5.44; event visible in Graylog stream pan-fw within 12s. Config commit event ID verified. Closed 2024-04-11.

Requirement 03.07.06 — Maintenance Personnel
03.07.06.d: Designate organizational personnel with required access authorizations and technical competence to supervise the maintenance activities of personnel who do not possess the required access authorizations.

Evidence excerpts:
--- [Maintenance_Escort_Procedure_v2.3.docx] (excerpt)
4.2 Supervising Uncleared Maintenance Personnel
Any vendor technician who does not hold a company Okta account and a signed access agreement, including Haas, Mazak, and HVAC field service staff, must be escorted for the entire visit by a Designated Maintenance Supervisor (DMS). A DMS must (a) hold an active Okta account in the group "CUI-Authorized", (b) have completed the annual CUI handling course, and (c) be qualified on the equipment being serviced, meaning a Level 2 Machine Maintenance certification for CNC controllers or IT Systems Administrator for servers and network gear. The DMS stays within line of sight of the technician, connects or disconnects network cables on the technician's behalf, and checks that no removable media leaves the site until it has been scanned. The Facilities Manager and IT Manager review the DMS roster every quarter.

4.2 Encryption of Remote Sessions
All remote connections to the Halvorsen Composites network must terminate on the FortiGate 60F SSL VPN using FortiClient 7.2 or later. Remote administration of endpoints is done only through NinjaOne remote control, which uses TLS-encrypted relay sessions. RDP from the internet to company hosts is not allowed and is blocked at the firewall.

The IT Administrator checks the VPN cipher configuration every quarter and records the result in Zendesk.

4.2 Approved Cryptographic Mechanisms for Remote Sessions
All remote connections into the Fennwick Microelectronics network go through the Cisco Meraki MX250 at the Dayton plant using AnyConnect client VPN. The following mechanisms are approved for protecting session confidentiality:
- Tunnel protocol: TLS 1.2 or higher with DTLS 1.2 for the data channel. SSL VPN and L2TP/IPsec are disabled.
- Cipher suites: AES-256-GCM (preferred) and AES-128-GCM. CBC-mode ciphers, 3DES and RC4 are prohibited.
- Key exchange: ECDHE (P-256/P-384), which provides perfect forward secrecy.
- Server certificate: RSA 3072-bit, issued by DigiCert, renewed every year.
Administrative SSH to network gear uses only aes256-gcm@openssh.com and chacha20-poly1305. Owner: IT Infrastructure Manager. The standard is reviewed every year, or sooner if NIST deprecates an algorithm.

Evidence excerpts:
--- [Configuration_Change_Management_Procedure_v3.2.docx] (excerpt)
5.4 Post-Implementation Monitoring and Review
Every approved change in Freshservice (Change type: Normal or Emergency) has to be correlated against Splunk Cloud activity within 2 business days of implementation. The Change Coordinator runs the saved search "CHG-Correlation-Daily". It compares pfSense config.xml diffs, Jamf Pro configuration profile and policy edits, Okta admin system log events, and Sophos Central policy modifications against open and recently closed change records. Any modification with no matching CHG number is flagged as unauthorized and opened as a Security Incident within 4 hours. The Change Advisory Board (IT Operations Manager, ISSO, and one research computing representative) meets every Tuesday. At that meeting the board reviews the prior week's closed changes, any rollbacks, and correlation exceptions. Minutes are attached to the Freshservice CAB problem record.
--- [splunk_savedsearch_CHG-Correlation-Daily_export.txt] (excerpt)

4.2 Sanitization Methods. Before any system media that has stored CUI (laptop SSDs, workstation HDDs, USB drives, Datto SIRIS appliance drives, optical-test-bench controller disks) leaves Quillfeather Software's control or is reissued, the IT Operations Lead must make sure it is sanitized to NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 1 standards. 4.2 Reassignment of CUI-Bearing Endpoints
Before a MacBook or Windows laptop from the Program Engineering or Contracts groups goes back into the spare pool, the IT Asset Coordinator must:
(a) Issue the Jamf Pro 'Wipe Computer' command (Erase All Content and Settings on Apple silicon/T2 devices). This is a cryptographic erase.

Requirement 03.04.03 — Configuration Change Control
03.04.03.b: Review proposed configuration-controlled changes to the system, and approve or disapprove such changes with explicit consideration for security impacts.

Evidence excerpts:
--- [GE-ITP-014_Configuration_Change_Control_Procedure_v3.2.docx] (excerpt)
4.3 Change Advisory Board (CAB) Review. Every Normal and Major change to an in-scope CUI system needs CAB review before work starts. The CAB meets every Tuesday at 10:00 ET. Voting members are the IT Operations Manager (chair), the Information Security Lead, the Infrastructure Engineer on rotation and the owner of the affected system. Quorum is three members, and the Information Security Lead must be one of them. Before scheduling, the requester fills in the Security Impact Analysis (SIA) section of the ServiceNow change form. The SIA asks which security controls the change affects, whether CUI data flows change, the rollback plan and whether the SSP or baseline must be updated. The CAB records its decision in ServiceNow as Approved, Approved with Conditions or Rejected, with a written reason. If the SIA risk rating is High, the Information Security Lead must sign off explicitly, and that person can block the change alone.

4.3 Interactive Logon to Privileged Accounts
Every interactive console logon with a privileged account (Domain Admins, Server Admins, Workstation Admins, and the tier-0 'adm-' accounts) must use two factors. 4.3 Password History
All Active Directory accounts in the GRAYWACKE.LOCAL domain, including standard users, privileged admin (-a) accounts, and service accounts, must not reuse any of their previous 24 passwords. The setting is enforced technically through the Default Domain Policy and through Fine-Grained Password Policies for privileged groups. It is not left to users to follow on their own. Records tied to an open incident or legal hold stay until the Security Lead releases them in writing, and for at least 3 years. Each quarter, the IT Systems Admin restores the oldest archive and confirms legal holds remain.

4.2 Retention Periods
Audit records produced by in-scope systems are kept for the periods below. The IT Manager owns this table and reviews it every year.
- Wazuh indexer (hot, searchable): 90 days
- Wazuh archives (compressed, read-only): 1 year total from the event date
- Active Directory Security event logs forwarded via Wazuh agent: same as above
- FortiGate 60F traffic and event logs (sent to Wazuh by syslog): 1 year
- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint: 180 days in the portal, with alerts also exported to Wazuh for 1 year
- Google Workspace admin and login audit: exported every day to Wazuh, 1 year
Records that relate to an open incident or legal hold are kept until the Security Lead releases them in writing, and in any case for at least 3 years.
